answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation something grown, not bought: every identity tends a small garden of work, and each contribution is sealed like a walnut — a hash of the work plus the previous seal, forming a chain that cannot be rewritten or copied. New identities may only take tiny jobs, and larger work unlocks only after verified contributions spaced over real calendar days, so a farmer cannot forge ten histories in parallel overnight. Copying another chain fails because seals reference its own keys, and buying an old garden costs more than the jobs it unlocks.
